messages:
maria.g: Quick follow-up on the API key scoping RFC — can we pick a clear pattern for service->service auth? we keep circling between long-lived project keys vs ephemeral delegation tokens.

tanner: My short take: prefer short-lived delegated tokens for S2S where possible. long-lived project keys should be reserved for human/CI uses. tradeoffs: rotation, complexity, and audit surface.

jean: Agreed. We should make the delegated token map to an explicit actor (actor_id + parent_key) so RBAC checks remain exact. audit logs need to show both the delegator and the actor.

samir: One ops constraint: some customers in Private on-prem want zero outbound calls. brokered ephemeral tokens mean we need an in-VPC broker or allow local minting with signed attestations.

tanner: Right — design option A: token-broker service (hosted + optional on-prem agent). option B: signed delegation JWTs minted by the parent key and verified offline.

maria.g: Option B seems attractive for offline but we need revocation. signed JWTs are hard to revoke without a broker.

tanner: True. compromise: short TTL signed tokens (e.g., 5m-15m) + optional revocation list for enterprise. default: broker for hosted customers, signed tokens for private/air-gapped with shorter TTL.

jean: For RBAC surface we should add a new token claim: "delegation_chain": ["key:proj:123","svc:actor:xyz"] and an explicit "actor" claim. also add "orig_key_id" for audit.

samir: We need to think about SDK ergonomics. C#/.js/py SDKs should expose a simple API: auth.delegate(parent_key, target_actor, ttl) that returns usable header.

maria.g: Example header sketch:

```
Authorization: Redwood-Key key=sr-abcdef1234
X-Redwood-Delegation: v1;token=eyJhbGci...
```

or inline: Authorization: Redwood-Delegated eyJ...

tanner: Also flagging backward compatibility: any new header must fall back to existing project-key semantics if validation fails. we can't break existing callers.

jean: Auditing: when a delegated token is used we log: {time, endpoint, delegator_key_id, actor_id, delegation_token_id, verification_method}. make sure this is consumable by the console (per-route cost/latency traces).

samir: Security: rotate parent keys frequently and require attestation for the delegator service (mTLS or signed service identity) to be allowed to mint delegations. enterprise customers can enforce additional policies.

tanner: Migration plan (rough):
- phase 0: add token validation support and logging in runtime (no changes to issuance). feature flag off by default.
- phase 1: SDK helper + server-side broker implementation behind flag. enable for internal services.
- phase 2: invite early customers to opt-in to brokered delegation; collect metrics.
- phase 3: default to brokered for hosted, enable signed-delegation for private by config.

maria.g: metrics to capture: delegation token issuance rate, token TTL distribution, auth failures by delegation vs direct keys, and increase in per-route latency.

jean: One more: RBAC policy language extension to reference delegation_chain and require explicit "allow_delegation: true" on role bindings to avoid silent privilege escalation.

samir: Edge case: proxies that terminate TLS and forward requests — they need to preserve original actor claim. we should add guidance in the docs and SDK.

infra-bot: deploy status: auth-runtime v2.8 branch created, adding delegation validation hooks — build queued.

maria.g: OK. action items: jean will draft follow-up RFC with claims and audit fields; tanner will prototype broker and signed JWT paths; samir will draft SDK API surface and doc changes. I'll open a tracking ticket and add the migration phases.

tanner: sgtm :+1:

jean: I'll put a PR up by EOD Thurs for the claim shape.

samir: I'll mock SDK usage in the repo and add unit tests for TTL edge cases.

maria.g: thanks all — we'll reconvene after the RFC PR. :rocket:
